Microsoft attributed the lower Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage (to 69%) to the impact of scaling its AI infrastructure, partly offset by efficiency gains in Azure. Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 23% to $168.9 billion, and Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 34%. Company-wide, gross margin slipped from about 69.8% to about 68.8% (down about 0.94 percentage points). Operating margin rose from about 44.6% to about 45.6%, so the squeeze showed up in gross margin and not in operating margin. The filing does not give figures that split the margin change into its separate drivers.
Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9 billion in FY2025, and Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 34%.
Microsoft said the Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 69%, driven by the impact of scaling its AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure. It also said cost of revenue increased $13.7 billion, or 19%, driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud.
In the Intelligent Cloud segment, cost of revenue rose $10.6 billion, or 36%, driven by growth in Azure. The segment gross margin percentage decreased because of AI infrastructure scaling, offset in part by Azure efficiency gains.
In Productivity and Business Processes, the gross margin percentage decreased slightly, primarily driven by the impact of scaling AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud.
Company-wide revenue grew about 14.9% in FY2025, from $245.1 billion to $281.7 billion.
Company-wide gross margin was about 69.8% in FY2024.
Company-wide gross margin was about 68.8% in FY2025.
Company-wide gross margin fell by about 0.94 percentage points from FY2024 to FY2025.
Company-wide operating margin was about 44.6% in FY2024.
Company-wide operating margin was about 45.6% in FY2025.
Company-wide operating margin rose by about 0.98 percentage points from FY2024 to FY2025.
